Definition: Percentage of individuals who used the internet (from any location, via any device) in the last three months. This measures actual internet adoption beyond network availability, capturing the combined effect of infrastructure, affordability, digital literacy, and relevance.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: ITU/World Bank data (via FRED series ITNETUSERP2LBY, sourced from ITU) show internet users at 82.1% of population in 2023 and 81.95% in 2024, consistent with ITU DataHub's 82% (2024) figure and with DataReportal's own later reports (88.4% in 2024, 88.5% in 2025). The cited Digital 2023 figure of 45.9% is a clear outlier against this consistent 74-82% series for 2020-2024 and appears to be a data or methodology error in that single Kepios report. Revised to code 5 (70%+) on the stronger, corroborated ITU/World Bank series.

Comments: ITU GCI score 68.09, third level maturity
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed: ITU's Global Cybersecurity Index 2024 (press release corroborated by an independent aggregator, statbase.org) gives Libya a score of 68.09, placing it in Tier 2 'Advancing', up from 28.78 in 2020. This falls within the 60-79 band, so the original code 4 is correct and now backed by more than one source.

redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: World Bank/IEA Tracking SDG7 data put Libya's electricity access rate at 73.2% in 2023 (up from 70.0% in 2022), corroborated independently by TheGlobalEconomy.com and the Tracking SDG7 database. This falls in the 50-74% band, not the 75-89% band originally coded; revised down to code 3.

revision_notes: The original comment already names three hubs (Tatweer/Benghazi, Asarya, Silphium Labs), and further verification found at least three more with documented regular activity: Innovation Garden IG (Tripoli accelerator), the EU/UNDP-backed Isnaed Tripoli Centre Business Incubator, and the government SME agency's ICT and other sectoral business incubators.
